claim: The FTC's Rule on the Use of Consumer Reviews and Testimonials took effect on October 21, 2024.
evidence: This rule is effective October 21, 2024.

claim: The rule addresses fake reviews and testimonials, buying positive or negative reviews, undisclosed insider reviews, company-controlled review sites, certain review suppression, and fake social media influence indicators.
evidence: prohibits selling or purchasing fake consumer reviews or testimonials, buying positive or negative consumer reviews, certain insiders creating consumer reviews

claim: 16 CFR 465.1 defines a consumer review as a consumer's evaluation, or a purported consumer's evaluation, of a product, service, or business.
evidence: a consumer's evaluation, or a purported consumer's evaluation, of a product, service, or business

claim: 16 CFR 465.2(a) makes it unlawful for a business to write, create, or sell a consumer review or testimonial that misrepresents the reviewer or their experience.
evidence: for a business to write, create, or sell a consumer review, consumer testimonial, or celebrity testimonial

claim: 16 CFR 465.2(b) prohibits a business from purchasing such a consumer review, or disseminating such a testimonial, which it knew or should have known materially misrepresented the reviewer or experience.
evidence: for a business to purchase a consumer review, or to disseminate or cause the dissemination of a consumer testimonial ... which the business knew or should have known materially misrepresented
verifier_note: Corrected: 465.2(b) text says 'purchase' a review / 'disseminate' a testimonial; 'procure' removed. Checked against regulatory text in FR 2024-18519.

claim: 16 CFR 465.2(d) exempts reviews resulting from generalized solicitations to purchasers and reviews that appear because the business merely engages in consumer review hosting.
evidence: making generalized solicitations to purchasers to post reviews or testimonials ... merely engaging in consumer review hosting.

claim: 16 CFR 465.4 prohibits compensation or incentives in exchange for, or conditioned expressly or by implication on, a review expressing a particular sentiment.
evidence: to provide compensation or other incentives in exchange for, or conditioned expressly or by implication on ... expressing a particular sentiment

claim: 16 CFR 465.5(a) bars an officer or manager from writing a consumer review without a clear and conspicuous disclosure of their material relationship.
evidence: an officer or manager of a business to write or create a consumer review ... clear and conspicuous disclosure

claim: 16 CFR 465.5(c) addresses soliciting or demanding reviews from immediate relatives or from employees or agents of the business.
evidence: to solicit or demand a consumer review about the business ... from any of their immediate relatives or from any employee or agent

claim: 16 CFR 465.6 prohibits misrepresenting that a website or entity the business controls, owns, or operates provides independent reviews or opinions.
evidence: that a website, organization, or entity that it controls, owns, or operates provides independent reviews or opinions

claim: 16 CFR 465.7(a) covers an unfounded or groundless legal threat, a physical threat, intimidation, or a public false accusation in response to a consumer review.
evidence: use an unfounded or groundless legal threat, a physical threat, intimidation, or a public false accusation
verifier_note: Completed: added 'unfounded or groundless legal threat', which is in the 465.7(a) text.

claim: 16 CFR 465.7(b) prohibits misrepresenting displayed reviews when reviews are suppressed based on ratings or negative sentiment; its exceptions cover trade secrets or confidential information, defamatory or harassing content, others' personal information, discriminatory content, clearly false content, reviews reasonably believed fake, and wholly unrelated reviews.
evidence: The seller reasonably believes the review is fake ... The review is wholly unrelated to the products or services offered
verifier_note: Corrected: page listed only 3 of the 7 exceptions in 465.7(b); full list now given.

claim: 16 CFR 465.8 prohibits selling or distributing, and purchasing or procuring, fake indicators of social media influence that the person knew or should have known to be fake.
evidence: Sell or distribute fake indicators of social media influence that they knew or should have known to be fake ... Purchase or procure fake indicators
verifier_note: Claim widened to 465.8(b) because the page sentence also covers procurement.

claim: The FTC states the rule will enable the Commission to seek civil penalties against violators.
evidence: As an additional benefit, the rule will enable the Commission to seek civil penalties against violators.

claim: 16 CFR 1.98(d) lists $53,088 as the maximum civil penalty for section 5(m)(1)(A) of the FTC Act, applying to penalties assessed after January 17, 2025.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: (d) Section 5(m)(1)(A) of the FTC Act, 15 U.S.C. 45(m)(1)(A)—$53,088; ... apply only to penalties assessed after January 17, 2025
verifier_note: eCFR 1.98 (up to date as of 7/13/2026) shows $53,088 at (d), amounts apply to penalties assessed after January 17, 2025 [90 FR 5581]. FTC notice 2026-18853 (Sept 15, 2026) keeps 2025 levels for 2026.

claim: Part 465 contains sections 465.2, 465.4, 465.5, 465.6, 465.7 and 465.8 with the headings shown in the table.
evidence: § 465.4 Buying positive or negative consumer reviews. § 465.6 Company-controlled review websites or entities. § 465.7 Review suppression.

claim: Under 16 CFR 255.5(a), material connections must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously and can include payment or free or discounted products.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: such connection must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously ... They can include monetary payment or the provision of free or discounted products

claim: Under 16 CFR 255.5(a), the disclosure must communicate the nature of the connection sufficiently for consumers to evaluate its significance.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: it must clearly communicate the nature of the connection sufficiently for consumers to evaluate its significance.
